article: C++でAI推論エンジンを考える
scope: Rewrote the Japanese article and twelve translations to scope it as an architecture overview, not a working LLM engine. Checked C++ versus Python claims, deployment caveats, arena allocation/deallocation and alignment, reset/object lifetime, weight-memory arithmetic, quantization overhead and quality caveats, backend claims, and current upstream/API references.
findings: Changed the title and opening to disclose that the original snippets did not form a complete or runnable inference engine and included no model loader, tokenizer, full Transformer, sampling, full GPU backend, or benchmark.
Removed unqualified claims that C++ automatically eliminates Python overhead, makes deployment a single binary, always improves performance, or that inference has a fixed 90% GEMM share.

Replaced the platform-specific allocator with a C++17 aligned byte arena that checks capacity and alignment, pairs aligned allocation/deallocation, disables copying, and documents destructor/lifetime limits.
Qualified quantization and backend claims; clarified decimal GB versus GiB and raw weights versus cache, metadata, and workspace.
Aligned all 13 locales and added current upstream GGML/llama.cpp and official CUDA, Apple, and WG21 references.

meaning.note: Aligned the revised scope: conceptual architecture and an arena example, not a complete LLM inference implementation or performance claim.

terminology.note: Checked tensors, KV cache, memory arena, FP32/FP16/INT8/INT4, CUDA/cuBLAS, Metal Performance Shaders, and C++17 aligned allocation terminology.

mathematics.note: Verified the 7e9 FP32 weight estimate, decimal GB vs GiB, raw bit-width ratios, and explicit exclusion of metadata/cache/workspace.

code.note: Compiled and ran the C++17 arena with MSVC: checked matching aligned allocation/deallocation, disabled copying, 16/64-byte alignment, reset reuse, invalid-alignment rejection, capacity failure, and the documented destructor limitation.

links.note: Added primary GGML/llama.cpp, NVIDIA cuBLAS, Apple Metal Performance Shaders, and WG21 C++ working-draft references.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.

Performance, quantization quality, and memory fit are workload- and hardware-dependent; readers must test their model, build, and target device.
